## Design

### 2026-10-12 – ### What I worked on

**4h**

### What I worked on
Modeled and verified the primary two-piece protective enclosure for the SmartCurtain controller, designing both the main chassis and the top lid to house the pcb and the stepper motor

### CAD Assembly and PCB footprint referencing
  - Imported the 3D STEP model exported from KiCad into the CAD workspace to extract precise component bounding boxes, connector alignments, and standoff pitches.
  - Applied a 0.35mm horizontal clearance offset between the PCB perimeter and internal enclosure walls to account for FDM thermal shrinkage and board fabrication tolerances.

### Main Bottom Enclosure
  - Parameterized structural wall thickness to 2.4mm (ensuring an exact multiple of 6 solid perimeters with a 0.4mm nozzle for maximum rigidity).
  - Modeled 4 external cylindrical screw pillars with countersunk bores sized for M3 fasteners and brass heat-set threaded inserts.
  - Integrated lower terminal access windows for all 4 screw terminal blocks (stepper phases and sensor interfaces) using 45-degree peaked roofs, completely eliminating the need for internal support material during 3D printing.
  - Created a recessed cutout for the USB-C port with a 1.0mm relief pocket to ensure wide USB-C cable overmolds seat fully into the receptacle.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/32fff56f6c89cf9a9a509fd416cc052d4bf0556de88415043d3acc6b7927679b.png)

### Top Enclosure Lid
  - Modeled a dedicated top shell with self-aligning recessed mating lips to interface securely with the bottom chassis.
  - Added directional ventilation slots directly above the TMC2209 StepStick socket to enable passive convective airflow across the driver heatsink.
  - Placed concentric pass-through cutouts for the EC11 rotary encoder control shaft and the 5mm 940nm IR emitter LED.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/ed511435a94c52bb74fb88ac630955ac7379a053356b573f34dc71bb3ae29288.png)

### What broke and how I fixed it
- Rectangular terminal block cutouts originally required fragile support structures that would have been tedious to clean out; redesigned the upper edge of every side opening with 45-degree chamfers so the slicer can bridge cleanly without any print supports.
-Sharp right-angle junctions between the corner mounting pillars and the main outer walls showed high shear stress risks; added generous filleted ribs along the pillar seams to prevent layer delamination under fastener torque.

### Next steps
Model the NEMA17 bracket

### 2026-10-13 – ### What I worked on

**3.8h**

### What I worked on
Implemented a major mechanical architecture overhaul in enclosure model v4, transitioning from a split layout to a compact, vertically integrated unibody chassis (~95 × 66 × 76 mm) housing both the PCB and the NEMA stepper motor in a unified vertical stack.

### Vertical Integration
  - Repositioned the stepper motor directly underneath the PCB, coupled via 30mm M3 hex standoffs
  - Reduced top lid clearance to 17mm above the PCB
  - Configured motor mounting orientation with front face M3 threads facing the PCB, dedicating the intermediate inter-board envelope to the transmission mechanism

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/4379bdd2be4243c9484fdfa9c9fc588e934f316666cfa1a4dc9376ea5a27fcfe.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/868e83a677b3e5e0c7cfe4da49d91ed21a8eeac3416a55d8a9d9943f2df99230.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/10af434b6c1da2eec7b2e5e7eb2e566ba4dba80819b456cdb22f751e7d34a1d0.png)

### Wiring Pass-Throughs and Internal Motor Routing
  - Integrated dedicated cable egress slots for external screw terminals
  - Removed external openings on the stepper terminal

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/c2d967cd636f66a3227a0855bcf20052e1dd6eb3738f055c2cdc6de73aac3abd.png)

### What broke and how I fixed it
- Relocating the stepper motor moved the bottom TMC2209 vent grilles 57mm below the PCB; noted that wall mounting obstructs bottom convective airflow, necessitating optimized top lid vents and adequate duty-cycle limits on the driver holding current.
- Initial motor placement risked shorting against sharp through-hole solder tails on the bottom layer; resolved by setting standoff height to 30mm, creating a safe 26.5mm clearance buffer beyond the longest 3.5mm leads.

### 2026-10-14 – ### Idler Pulley and Belt Tensioner

**4.5h**

### Idler Pulley and Belt Tensioner

This session was focused on designing the belt tensioner mechanism

The 3D model is split into four printable parts laid out on the build plate: the stationary wall bracket, the sliding carriage, the flanged idler pulley, and a small spacer sleeve

### What I worked on
- I designed the fixed mount with a female dovetail channel and two triangular support ribs on the back wall to handle the pulling force of the belt. It includes side holes for wall screws and a central hole on the back plate for an M3 tensioning screw
- I modeled a sliding fork with a male dovetail shape on the back. It holds an M3 heat-set insert and moves smoothly along the bracket to adjust belt tension in place
- I made a pulley with side flanges to keep the timing belt from slipping off. The inside has stepped pockets to pressfit two miniature ball bearings
- I added a small sleeve to fit an M3 bolt neatly through the center of the bearings

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/7bb7e722ae5923df06fbe12dac334835ac68f74a75394d8968bcc1dff686dc8e.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/a68c35eb4805fac5365d092187475e61808193ce2d8b67795df106be384e096b.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/9ed57a4128536a6f45d60f8ef07aaf352221ec3b755c5753e07e1ddd45df901e.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/f62dccb4f8e215e2935261750e89e04b73ff1384eb8792e7b15d4e874ff224c9.png)

### What worked and what didn't:
**What worked**
  - The dovetail angle is self-supporting, so all parts can be 3D printed flat or upright without support material
  - The M3 threaded insert sits inside the carriage block so the tensioning screw pulls against solid plastic, preventing the insert from ripping out under belt load.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/1ada5b3d5736bdafc8ccc12c7011146cf862c4d32d692f1b834c599ba6956457.png)

**Challenges and fixes**
  - Standard 3D printed holes shrink slightly, so I added a +0.1 mm tolerance to the bearing seats so the two bearings can be pressed in snugly without cracking the plastic
  - I added a 0.2 mm clearance on the dovetail slides so the carriage glides smoothly without wobbling or getting stuck

### 2026-10-15 – In this work session on SmartCurtai, I focused on the design and parametric modeling of the four main mechanical components for motion transmission, sensor mounting, and manual control of the user int

**3.5h**

In this work session on SmartCurtai, I focused on the design and parametric modeling of the four main mechanical components for motion transmission, sensor mounting, and manual control of the user interface:

### 1. Belt-to-Curtain Trolley Carrier
- The central carriage that slides along the track and acts as the mechanical core of the curtain motion system
- It firmly clamps both open ends of the GT2 timing belt using 14 internal molded teeth, converting the rotational motion from the stepper motor into linear movement
- It includes a smooth longitudinal bypass tunnel so the opposite return belt span can run freely through without rubbing or friction
- It provides a reinforced front eyelet to attach the lead curtain hook, pulling the curtain fabric along the rail during opening and closing cycles
 - The top surface incorporates a female dovetail slot and an M3 heat-set insert pocket to lock the track adapter securely in place

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/f04910b56ffeb82e5abf5bd21421d06c7d58ee4ea89cb94fb697e6b9d6d5dd40.png)

### 2. Modular Track Adapter
- An interchangeable sliding glider that fits directly inside the profile of the curtain rail
- It mates to the carrier via a male dovetail joint and an M3 screw, providing complete modularity. The entire system can adapt to different track geometries by swapping just this single part without reprinting the main carrier

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/7a246c9e0422f203d5234fffdb5caf457b62441ffecce5e46e5b420642e5ae2f.png)

### 3. Angled mmWave Sensor Mount
- A wedge-shaped bracket with a fixed downward tilt featuring an internal pocket and slotted M3 mounting ears
- It houses the HLK-LD2410 used for room occupancy tracking and presence automation

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/89681b5e2d26726b107349f552499e819922c56f67e837ca7408201afbecd057.png)

### 4. Custom EC11 Knob
- It serves as the physical interface on the main controller enclosure, letting the user turn the encoder to adjust curtain position/speed or press it to toggle states

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/c757c1a9b50e926c0456b419945e5b6c336c890d76f59982112e84c1876cc5e7.png)

### 2026-10-16 – ### 1. What I worked on:

**1.5h**

### 1. What I worked on:
- Designed a precise cylindrical bore with an optional D-shaft flat profile
- Added a bottom clamping collar featuring a transverse M3 screw hole and an internal M3 hex-nut retention pocket, allowing a grub screw or bolt to clamp securely onto the motor's flat shaft surface without slipping.
- Modeled a 20-tooth GT2 timing profile with a 2mm pitch, optimized for standard 6mm wide openended GT2 belts.
- Incorporated upper and lower side flanges with internal 30° lead-in chamfers to prevent the timing belt from walking off or derailing during hightorque movements.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/56b2135370478f1e91a59284b656d925e573d121869f27854ccdd136d235d1c0.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/6015892331cf3a55d24e776a65b53a1acd13b9421425f5eb1e332b385673ddd4.png)

### 2026-10-17 – ### What I made

**4.5h**

### What I made
In this session, I reviewed all the 3D models.

- I Checked the alignment and fit between all the different printed parts and hardware.
- Realized there were several compatibility and clearance issues across the parts when trying to assemble them together.
- Modified and updated the CAD files to fix these conflicts and make sure everything is fully compatible.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/6cd82637d79768f8360d55fd8bc72ceaf69ed9f74e35d78714ef1c814a75f7b9.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/43d8de11bf86dbecadf590fffed1a05bb65dba81073526ec13d8eac093fcba14.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/6a22df77f04b7d741e00d5f39208047ba357f4bf524f466754d5e9f2ad2f780c.png)

### Issues
- The parts looked fine individually, but inspecting the full assembly revealed several dimensional mismatches, tight clearances, and misaligned holes that wouldn't have assembled properly.
- Updated the models to clean up those interferences so the pieces mate and slide correctly.

### Next steps
Work on 3d printer slicing parameters (like infill, walls, speed...) and make some print profiles for most used 3d printers
